a07.salok: Salok. That Supreme Lord is beyond reach and beyond measure. Whoever speaks of him is set free. Listen, friend, Nanak humbly says: wondrous is the account of the Saadhs, the holy ones.
a07.p1: Ashtapadi. In the Saadh's company, faces become radiant. In the Saadh's company, all filth is washed away. In the Saadh's company, pride is erased. In the Saadh's company, true wisdom dawns. In the Saadh's company, one realises that God is near. In the Saadh's company, every conflict is settled. In the Saadh's company, one gains the jewel of the Naam, God's Name. In the Saadh's company, one's effort is directed to the One. What mortal can describe the greatness of the Saadh? O Nanak, the glory of the Saadh is merged in God.
a07.p2: In the Saadh's company, one meets the Lord who is beyond the senses. In the Saadh's company, one is ever in bloom. In the Saadh's company, the five passions come under control. In the Saadh's company, one savours the taste of nectar. In the Saadh's company, one becomes the dust under everyone's feet. In the Saadh's company, one's words become pleasing. In the Saadh's company, the mind does not run off anywhere. In the Saadh's company, the mind finds steadiness. In the Saadh's company, one stays apart from Maya, the world's illusion and wealth. In the Saadh's company, O Nanak, God is well pleased.
a07.p3: In the Saadh's company, all enemies become friends. In the Saadh's company, one becomes supremely pure. In the Saadh's company, one bears enmity towards no one. In the Saadh's company, the feet do not stray onto a crooked path. In the Saadh's company, no one seems bad. In the Saadh's company, one comes to know supreme bliss. In the Saadh's company, the fever of ego is gone. In the Saadh's company, one gives up all sense of self. God himself knows the greatness of the Saadh. O Nanak, the Saadh and God are at one.
a07.p4: In the Saadh's company, one never goes astray. In the Saadh's company, one finds lasting peace. In the Saadh's company, one attains that which is beyond the senses. In the Saadh's company, one bears the unbearable. In the Saadh's company, one dwells in the highest place. In the Saadh's company, one reaches God's mansion. In the Saadh's company, every righteous duty takes firm root. In the Saadh's company, one's attention rests on the Supreme Lord alone. In the Saadh's company, one gains the treasure of the Naam. Nanak is a sacrifice to the Saadh.
a07.p5: In the Saadh's company, one redeems one's whole family line. In the Saadh's company, one carries loved ones, friends and family across. In the Saadh's company, one obtains that wealth by which everyone is blessed. In the Saadh's company, Dharam Rai, the judge of souls, serves one. In the Saadh's company, the gods sing one's praise. In the Saadh's company, sins take flight. In the Saadh's company, the nectar-sweet praises of God are sung. In the Saadh's company, every place is within reach. O Nanak, in the Saadh's company, one's birth bears fruit.
a07.p6: In the Saadh's company, no toil at all is needed; on simply beholding the Saadh, one is filled with bliss. In the Saadh's company, all stains are taken away. In the Saadh's company, hell is left far behind. In the Saadh's company, one is at ease here and hereafter. In the Saadh's company, those separated are united with the Lord. Whatever one longs for, that very fruit one receives. In the Saadh's company, no one goes away empty-handed. The Supreme Lord dwells in the heart of the Saadh. O Nanak, one is saved by hearing the Saadh's words and delighting in them.
a07.p7: In the Saadh's company, I hear the Lord's Name. In the Saadh's company, I sing the Lord's praises. In the Saadh's company, God does not slip from the mind. In the Saadh's company, one is surely carried across. In the Saadh's company, God feels sweet. In the Saadh's company, he is seen in every heart. In the Saadh's company, we have become obedient to God. In the Saadh's company, we have been set free. In the Saadh's company, all ailments have gone. O Nanak, the Saadh is met by good fortune.
a07.p8: The Vedas do not know the greatness of the Saadh; they describe only as much as they have heard. The praise of the Saadh is beyond the three qualities of Maya. The praise of the Saadh fills everything. The glory of the Saadh has no end. The glory of the Saadh is boundless for ever. The glory of the Saadh is higher than the highest. The glory of the Saadh is greater than the greatest. The glory of the Saadh befits the Saadh alone. O Nanak, between the Saadh and God there is no distinction, brother.
a08.salok: Salok. He has the True One in his mind and that same True One on his lips; he sees no one but the One. O Nanak, whoever bears these marks is a Brahm Giani, one who knows God.
a08.p1: Ashtapadi. The Brahm Giani is ever unattached, as the lotus stays untouched in the water. The Brahm Giani is ever without blemish, as the sun dries up all things yet stays untainted. The Brahm Giani looks on all alike, as the wind touches king and pauper the same. The Brahm Giani's patience never changes, like the earth: one man digs it, another anoints it with sandal paste. This is the Brahm Giani's quality, O Nanak, like the innate nature of fire.
a08.p2: The Brahm Giani is purer than the pure, as dirt does not cling to water. The Brahm Giani's mind is filled with light, like the sky above the earth. The Brahm Giani holds friend and foe alike. The Brahm Giani has no pride. The Brahm Giani is higher than the highest, yet in his own mind he is the lowliest of all. Those alone have become Brahm Gianis, O Nanak, whom God himself has made so.
a08.p3: The Brahm Giani is the dust under everyone's feet. The Brahm Giani has come to know the joy of the soul. The Brahm Giani is kind to all. The Brahm Giani never does anything bad. The Brahm Giani ever sees all with an equal eye. The Brahm Giani's glance rains nectar. The Brahm Giani is free of all bonds. The Brahm Giani's way of life is pure. The Brahm Giani's food is divine wisdom. O Nanak, the Brahm Giani's meditation is fixed on God.
a08.p4: The Brahm Giani rests his hope on the One alone. The Brahm Giani never perishes. The Brahm Giani is steeped in humility. The Brahm Giani delights in doing good to others. The Brahm Giani has no worldly entanglements. The Brahm Giani holds the wandering mind in check. To the Brahm Giani, whatever happens is good. The Brahm Giani is richly fruitful. In the company of the Brahm Giani, all are saved. O Nanak, by means of the Brahm Giani the whole world remembers God.
a08.p5: The Brahm Giani is dyed in the love of the One alone. The Brahm Giani has God abiding with him. The Brahm Giani's support is the Naam, God's Name. The Brahm Giani's family is the Naam. The Brahm Giani is awake for ever and ever. The Brahm Giani casts off the ego-bound intellect. The Brahm Giani's mind holds supreme bliss. The Brahm Giani's home is ever filled with joy. The Brahm Giani dwells in peace and poise. O Nanak, the Brahm Giani never perishes.
a08.p6: The Brahm Giani is the knower of God. The Brahm Giani loves the One alone. The Brahm Giani is free of worry. The Brahm Giani's counsel is pure. The Brahm Giani is one whom God himself makes so. The Brahm Giani's majesty is great. A sight of the Brahm Giani is gained by great good fortune. To the Brahm Giani one should give oneself in sacrifice again and again. The Brahm Giani is sought even by Shiva, the great lord. O Nanak, the Brahm Giani is himself the Supreme God.
a08.p7: The Brahm Giani's worth cannot be reckoned. The Brahm Giani holds everything within his mind. Who knows the secret of the Brahm Giani? To the Brahm Giani, salutations for ever. Of the Brahm Giani not even half a syllable can be spoken. The Brahm Giani is the Master of all. Who can tell the measure of the Brahm Giani? Only a Brahm Giani knows the state of a Brahm Giani. The Brahm Giani has no end and no limit. O Nanak, bow for ever to the Brahm Giani.
a08.p8: The Brahm Giani is the creator of the whole world. The Brahm Giani lives for ever and does not die. The Brahm Giani gives souls the way to liberation. The Brahm Giani is the perfect Being, the Maker of destiny. The Brahm Giani is the guardian of those who have none. The Brahm Giani's hand is over all. The whole visible creation belongs to the Brahm Giani. The Brahm Giani is himself the Formless Lord. The Brahm Giani's glory befits the Brahm Giani alone. O Nanak, the Brahm Giani is the Lord of all.
a09.salok: Salok. One who enshrines the Naam, God's Name, deep within the heart, who sees the Lord in everything, who bows to the Master every moment: O Nanak, such a one is the Apras, the one untouched by evil, and he carries all across.
a09.p1: Ashtapadi. Falsehood does not touch his tongue. In his mind is love for the sight of the Immaculate Lord. His eyes do not gaze at the beauty of another's wife. He serves the Saadh, the holy one, and loves the company of the saints. His ears do not listen to slander of anyone. He considers himself the worst of all. By the Guru's grace he casts off the poison of Maya. The desires of his mind depart from his mind. He has conquered his senses and is free of the five vices. O Nanak, among millions there is hardly one such Apras.
a09.p2: He alone is a Vaishnav, a devotee of Vishnu, with whom God is well pleased; he stays apart from the Maya of Vishnu, the all-pervading Lord. While doing his deeds, he stays free of their bondage; pure is the faith of such a Vaishnav. He wishes for no reward of any kind. He is absorbed only in devotion and Kirtan, the singing of God's praises. Within his mind and body is the Simran, the remembrance, of the Lord of the world. He is kind to all. He holds firmly to the Naam himself and leads others to repeat it. O Nanak, such a Vaishnav attains the supreme state.
a09.p3: A Bhagauti, a worshipper of the Lord, is one imbued with love for devotion to the Lord. He forsakes all company of the wicked. All doubt is gone from his mind. He worships the Supreme Lord, knowing him to be in all. In the Saadh's company, he washes off the filth of sin. Such a Bhagauti's understanding becomes sublime. He serves the Lord constantly, day after day. He offers his mind and body in love of the all-pervading Lord. He enshrines the Lord's feet in his heart. O Nanak, such a Bhagauti attains the Lord.
a09.p4: That one is a Pandit, a learned man, who teaches his own mind; who seeks the Lord's Name within his own self; who drinks the sublime essence of the Lord's Name. Through that Pandit's teaching the world finds life. He keeps the Lord's praise in his heart; such a Pandit does not enter the womb again. He understands the root of the Vedas, the Puranas and the Simritis. He knows the manifest to lie within the unmanifest. He gives teaching to all four castes. O Nanak, to that Pandit, salutations for ever.
a09.p5: The seed mantra is wisdom for all. Among the four castes, anyone may meditate on the Naam. Whoever meditates on it is liberated. In the Saadh's company, some rare person obtains it. By his grace, God enshrines it deep within the heart. It carries across even beasts, ghosts, fools and the stone-hearted. The Naam is the remedy for every ailment. Singing God's praises is the very form of well-being and joy. It is not obtained by any technique or by any religious rite. O Nanak, it is obtained by one for whom it was written from the beginning, by God's grace.
a09.p6: One in whose mind the Supreme Lord dwells: his name is truly Ramdas, the Lord's servant. The Lord, the Soul of all, has come into his sight. He has found him in the spirit of a servant of servants. He knows the Lord to be ever near, very near. Such a servant is accepted in the Lord's court. God himself shows grace to his servant. That servant comes to understand everything. Amid all, his soul stays detached. Such, O Nanak, is the way of the Ramdas.
a09.p7: One who, in his soul, loves God's command is called Jivan Mukat, liberated while alive. To him joy is the same as sorrow. He is ever in bliss; there is no separation there. To him gold is the same as dust. Nectar is the same as bitter poison. Honour is the same as scorn. A beggar is the same as a king. Whatever God brings about, that is his way. O Nanak, that person is called Jivan Mukat.
a09.p8: All places belong to the Supreme Lord. In whatever home he places beings, such is the name they bear. He himself is able to do and to cause all to be done. Whatever pleases God, that in the end comes to pass. He himself has spread out, becoming endless waves. The ways of the Supreme Lord cannot be grasped. Such understanding as he gives, such is one's light. The Supreme Lord, the Creator, is imperishable. He is merciful for ever, for ever, for ever. Those who remember him in Simran again and again, O Nanak, are filled with bliss.
a10.salok: Salok. Countless people sing his praises, but there is no end or limit to him. O Nanak, God has fashioned the creation in many ways and in countless forms.
a10.p1: Ashtapadi. Millions upon millions have become worshippers. Millions upon millions observe religious rites and customary duties. Millions upon millions have come to live at places of pilgrimage. Millions upon millions wander in the forests as renunciants. Millions upon millions are listeners to the Vedas. Millions upon millions are great ascetics. Millions upon millions fix their meditation within the self. Millions upon millions are poets who reflect on him in verse. Millions upon millions meditate on his ever-new Naam, God's Name. O Nanak, they do not find the Creator's limit.
a10.p2: Millions upon millions have become proud. Millions upon millions are blind and ignorant. Millions upon millions are hard-hearted misers. Millions upon millions are unsoftened, their souls utterly dry. Millions upon millions steal the wealth of others. Millions upon millions slander others. Millions upon millions toil after Maya, worldly wealth. Millions upon millions roam in foreign lands. Whatever you, God, set them to, to that they hold. O Nanak, the Creator alone knows the Creator's creation.
a10.p3: Millions upon millions are Siddhas, celibates and yogis. Millions upon millions are kings enjoying pleasures. Millions upon millions are the birds and snakes he has created. Millions upon millions are the stones and trees he has brought forth. Millions upon millions are the winds, waters and fires. Millions upon millions are the countries and the realms of the earth. Millions upon millions are the moons, suns and stars. Millions upon millions are the gods, demons and Indras with royal canopies over their heads. He holds the whole creation strung on his own thread. O Nanak, whoever pleases him, he carries across.
a10.p4: Millions upon millions are of the qualities of passion, darkness and purity. Millions upon millions are the Vedas, Puranas, Simritis and Shastras. Millions upon millions are the jewels and oceans he has made. Millions upon millions are creatures of every kind. Millions upon millions are those he has made long-lived. Millions upon millions are the hills and golden Merus that came to be. Millions upon millions are yakshas, kinnars and fiends. Millions upon millions are spirits, ghosts, swine and beasts of prey. He is close to all and distant from all. O Nanak, he himself, remaining detached, pervades everything.
a10.p5: Millions upon millions dwell in the nether worlds. Millions upon millions live in hell and in heaven. Millions upon millions are born, live and die. Millions upon millions go round through many births. Millions upon millions eat while simply sitting at ease. Millions upon millions toil until they are worn out. Millions upon millions are those he has made rich. Millions upon millions are anxious over Maya. Wherever he wills, there he keeps them. O Nanak, everything is in God's hands.
a10.p6: Millions upon millions have become detached from the world; their minds are lovingly fixed on the Lord's Name. Millions upon millions search for God; they find the Supreme Lord within their own selves. Millions upon millions thirst for the sight of God; the imperishable God has met them. Millions upon millions pray for the Satsang, the company of the true; they are dyed in the love of the Supreme Lord. Those with whom he himself is well pleased, O Nanak, are blessed, blessed for ever.
a10.p7: Millions upon millions are the sources of life and the regions of the world. Millions upon millions are the skies and universes. Millions upon millions are the incarnations that have come to be. In many ways he has unfolded creation. Many times he has spread out its expanse. For ever and ever he is the One, Ekankar, the one Creator. Millions upon millions he has made, of many kinds. From God they came forth, and into God they merge. No one knows his limit. O Nanak, that God is himself all in all.
a10.p8: Millions upon millions are servants of the Supreme Lord; their souls are lit up. Millions upon millions know the essence of reality; with their eyes they ever behold the One alone. Millions upon millions drink the nectar of the Naam; they become immortal and live for ever and ever. Millions upon millions sing the glories of the Naam; they are absorbed in the joy of the soul, in peace and poise. He keeps his servants in mind with every breath. O Nanak, they are the beloved of the Supreme God.
a11.salok: Salok. The One God is the cause of all creation; there is no second at all. Nanak is a sacrifice to him who is in the water, on the land, and in the space between earth and sky.
a11.p1: Ashtapadi. He does and causes all to be done, and is able to do all. Whatever pleases him, that alone will happen. In an instant he establishes and overthrows. He has no end or limit at all. By his Hukam, God's command, he has set up the earth and holds it without support. By his Hukam all comes forth, and in his Hukam it merges. By his Hukam there are dealings high and low. By his Hukam there are countless colours and kinds. Having made it all, he beholds his own greatness. O Nanak, he pervades all.
a11.p2: If it pleases God, a human being attains liberation. If it pleases God, he makes even stones float. If it pleases God, he keeps a being alive even without breath. If it pleases God, one speaks the Lord's praises. If it pleases God, he saves even the fallen. He himself acts and he himself deliberates. He himself is Master of this world and the next. The Knower of hearts plays and rejoices. As he pleases, he has the work done. O Nanak, no other comes into sight.
a11.p3: Say, what can be achieved by a human being? Whatever pleases him, that he makes one do. If it were in this man's hands, he would seize everything. Whatever pleases him, that alone he does. Unknowing, one is engrossed in the poison of Maya; if one knew, one would save oneself. Led astray by doubt, he runs in all ten directions; in an instant he goes round the four corners and comes back. Those to whom he, in his mercy, gives his devotion, O Nanak, merge in the Naam, God's Name.
a11.p4: In an instant he gives a kingdom to a lowly worm. The Supreme Lord cherishes the humble. One in whom nothing at all is seen, he instantly makes known in all ten directions. Whoever receives his blessing, the Lord of the world does not reckon his account. Soul and body, all is his capital. In every heart is the light of the perfect God. He himself has fashioned his own creation. Nanak lives by beholding his greatness.
a11.p5: The strength of this being is not in its own hands. The Master of all does and causes all to be done. The poor creature is bound to obey. Whatever pleases him, that in the end comes to pass. Sometimes one dwells in high estate, sometimes in low. Sometimes one is in sorrow, and sometimes one laughs in the delight of joy. Sometimes one is busy with slander and worry. Sometimes one is high in the heavens, sometimes in the nether world. Sometimes one becomes versed in reflection on God. O Nanak, God himself is the one who unites one with him.
a11.p6: Sometimes one dances in many ways. Sometimes one stays asleep day and night. Sometimes one is fearsome in great anger. Sometimes one becomes the dust under everyone's feet. Sometimes one sits as a great king. Sometimes one wears the guise of a lowly beggar. Sometimes one falls into ill repute. Sometimes one is called good, very good. As God keeps one, so one remains. By the Guru's grace, Nanak speaks the truth.
a11.p7: Sometimes one becomes a Pandit and gives discourses. Sometimes one keeps silence and sits in meditation. Sometimes one bathes on the banks of pilgrimage places. Sometimes, as a Siddha or a seeker, one speaks wisdom. Sometimes one becomes a worm, an elephant or a moth. Deluded, one wanders through countless species. Like an actor, one shows many forms. As it pleases God, so he makes one dance. Whatever pleases him, that alone happens. O Nanak, there is no second, no other.
a11.p8: Sometimes this being finds the Saadh Sangat, the company of the holy; from that place one never returns. Within, the light of divine wisdom shines; that place does not perish. Mind and body are imbued with the Naam, in the love of the One; they dwell for ever with the Supreme Lord. As water comes and blends with water, so one's light merges with the Light. The comings and goings are ended; rest is found. Nanak is ever a sacrifice to God.
a12.salok: Salok. The humble one lives in peace, having subdued the self and keeping low. The mighty and arrogant, O Nanak, rot away in their own pride.
a12.p1: Ashtapadi. One who holds within himself the pride of power is bound for hell and becomes a dog. One who thinks himself full of youth and beauty becomes a maggot in filth. One who calls himself a doer of good deeds is born and dies and wanders through many species. One who is proud of wealth and land is a fool, blind and ignorant. One in whose heart God, in his mercy, places humility, O Nanak, is liberated here and finds peace hereafter.
a12.p2: One grows rich and becomes proud, yet not even a straw goes with him. One puts his hope in large armies and men; in a moment he is destroyed. One thinks himself the strongest of all; in an instant he is reduced to ashes. The arrogant one cares for no one; Dharam Rai, the judge of souls, puts him to disgrace. One whose pride is erased by the Guru's grace: that person, O Nanak, is accepted in the Lord's court.
a12.p3: One may do millions of good deeds while holding on to ego; he gains only toil, and all of it is in vain. One may do many penances in pride; he is born again and again into hell and heaven. For all his many efforts, his soul does not soften; tell me, how can he reach the Lord's court? One who calls himself good: goodness never comes near him. One whose mind becomes the dust under everyone's feet, says Nanak, has a spotless name.
a12.p4: As long as one thinks that anything can be done by him, he has no peace at all. As long as he thinks that he is the doer of anything, he wanders through wombs and births. As long as he holds one man as enemy and another as friend, his mind is not steady. As long as he is lost in attachment to Maya, Dharam Rai punishes him. By God's grace the bonds break; by the Guru's grace, O Nanak, ego is shed.
a12.p5: Having earned a thousand, he sets off running after a hundred thousand. Satisfaction does not come; he keeps chasing Maya. He indulges in countless pleasures of corruption. He is not satisfied; he wears himself out and dies. Without contentment no one is fulfilled. Like the wishes of a dream, all his works are in vain. In the love of the Naam, God's Name, all peace is found. Only some rare person, by great good fortune, obtains it. He himself, he alone, does and causes all to be done. For ever and ever, O Nanak, meditate on the Lord.
a12.p6: The Creator alone does and causes all to be done. What decision lies in this creature's hands? As he casts his glance, so one becomes. That God himself is all in all. Whatever he made, he made in his own pleasure. He is apart from all, and present with all. He understands, he sees, he judges. He is himself one, and himself many. He neither dies nor perishes; he neither comes nor goes. O Nanak, he ever pervades all.
a12.p7: He himself teaches and he himself understands. He himself is blended with all. He himself has made his own expanse. Everything is his; he is the Doer. Tell me, can anything be apart from him? In every place and the spaces between, he is the One alone. He himself performs his own plays. He stages wonders of endless colour. He is within the mind, and holds the mind within himself. O Nanak, no one can state his worth.
a12.p8: True, true, true is God, the Master. By the Guru's grace some rare one describes him. True, true, true is he who made everything. Among millions, only some rare one has recognised him. Good, good, good is your form, exceedingly beautiful, infinite and incomparable. Pure, pure, pure is your Word; in every heart it is heard by the ears and spoken. Holy, holy, holy and pure is the one who, O Nanak, meditates on the Naam with love in the mind.
